title: Platform events, change data capture, and event-driven processing
objectives: Define custom platform events versus Change Data Capture change events using official Developer Guide meanings.
Choose Publish After Commit versus Publish Immediately and explain subscriber timing and lock risk.
Contrast event-driven processing with Queueable/Batch (APEX-011) and same-transaction DML (APEX-010).
Cite EventBus.publish immediately (150) from Execution Governors and Limits; mark other event allocations Needs verification if not on that page.
diagnostic_question: An ERP must hear every LAB_Shipment__c create/update/delete, and a custom 'allocator requested' signal must fire even if the order save later fails. CDC, custom platform event, or Queueable—and which publish behavior?
definition: Platform events are secure, scalable messages with custom fields that publishers emit and subscribers receive in near real time. Change Data Capture publishes predefined change events for record create, update, delete, and undelete on selected objects (AccountChangeEvent, Shipment__ChangeEvent). Event-driven processing decouples the writer from the consumer via the event bus instead of a same-transaction DML or a single Queueable worker. ([Platform Events Developer Guide](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_intro.htm); [Change Data Capture Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_objects_change_data_capture.htm); [Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))
why_it_matters: Teams confuse CDC (every record change, including ETL) with a custom event (only the signals you publish). Publish Immediately can notify subscribers before the parent save commits and can cause row locks. Interviewers listen for that split.
sixty_second_explanation: Airport operations: CDC is the baggage RFID—every time a LAB_ bag moves, a standard scan event fires. A custom platform event is a PA announcement you write ('allocator requested') with your own fields. Publish After Commit waits until the flight is actually closed; Publish Immediately is the PA firing even if the gate later cancels—useful for logs, dangerous for inventory. Subscribers can be Apex triggers, Flow, or Pub/Sub API. EventBus.publish for immediately-published events counts toward 150 per transaction on the governors page. This is not Queueable: many listeners, not one job Id.
deeper_explanation: The Platform Events Developer Guide describes platform events as secure, scalable messages that connect Salesforce and external apps. You define the event and add custom fields; publishers use Flow, Apex, or APIs; subscribers use Flow, Apex triggers, Pub/Sub API, or CometD. Event definitions are metadata; published messages are data on the bus. ([Platform Events intro](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_intro.htm); [Defining Your Custom Platform Event](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_define.htm))

Change Data Capture publishes change events for create, update, delete, and undelete. Names follow the object: AccountChangeEvent, or Shipment__ChangeEvent for Shipment__c. Enable objects in Setup; you do not invent the schema. CDC is available since API 44.0 for supported objects. ([Change Data Capture Events](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.platform_events.meta/platform_events/platform_events_objects_change_data_capture.htm))

Publish After Commit (default for many designs) emits the message only if the Apex transaction commits—aligned with APEX-010. Publish Immediately emits even if the transaction later rolls back. Architect guidance: Publish Immediately is useful for logging; using it for business data can let subscribers act on a save that never committed and can cause row locks if those subscribers DML the same rows. ([Apex Transactions](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_transaction.htm) for commit; mark extra lock examples Needs verification against current Platform Event Considerations.)

EventBus.publish for platform events configured to publish immediately counts toward a per-transaction ceiling of 150 on Execution Governors and Limits (same number sync and async). After-commit publishes are listed among DML-counted operations on that page. Do not invent daily event-bus allocations here—those live in Platform Event Allocations and must be re-read; mark Needs verification if you cannot open that table. ([Execution Governors and Limits](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_gov_limits.htm))

Event-driven processing is optional. Same-record updates belong in before-save Flow or the current transaction. One follow-up callout with a job Id is Queueable (APEX-011). CDC or a custom event is for one-to-many, often external, consumers that should not share the writer's governors.

mental_model.analogy: Airport operations: CDC is automatic baggage RFID scans; a custom platform event is a PA announcement you write; Publish After Commit waits for the flight to close; Publish Immediately is the PA firing even if the gate cancels.
useful_mapping: RFID scan on every bag move → CDC change event
PA script you author → custom platform event fields
ground crews with radios → Apex / Flow / Pub/Sub subscribers
one dispatcher with a ticket → Queueable (not the bus)
where_it_breaks: CDC fires for ETL and Batch updates too—not only UI clicks.
Replay windows and daily event allocations are edition-specific; do not invent hours or counts.
The airport analogy does not encode CometD vs Pub/Sub API internals.

telugu_glossary.telugu: Custom bus message with fields you define.
Automatic change event for create, update, delete, or undelete.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: CDC emits standard change events for create, update, delete, undelete on selected objects. A custom platform event is a message you define. Publish After Commit waits for the parent transaction; Publish Immediately can fire even if that save rolls back. EventBus.publish immediately is 150 per transaction. Many subscribers, not one Queueable.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I ask who must hear the signal. Every row change including Batch/ETL: CDC, accepting volume risk. A curated business signal: custom event fields as metadata. One callout worker: Queueable, not the bus. I default to After Commit so subscribers do not act on rolled-back LAB_ orders. I use Immediately only for logs or similar. I cite 150 EventBus.publish for immediate events and refuse to invent daily bus caps. Tests for event triggers are required before production deploy—the Guide says so.

terminology.plain: A message type you define on the bus.
terminology.precise: Custom event object with standard plus custom fields. Published from Apex, Flow, or API; subscribed by Apex, Flow, Pub/Sub, CometD.
terminology.non_example: A custom object insert is not an event publish.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: CDC change event: platform-defined schema for record changes.
terminology.boundary: Definition is metadata; payloads are data.

terminology.plain: Automatic change events for selected objects.
terminology.precise: Publishes create, update, delete, undelete. AccountChangeEvent; Custom__ChangeEvent. Enabled in Setup. API 44.0+.
terminology.non_example: A custom __e you authored is not CDC.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Outbound message: older point-to-point, not the event bus.
terminology.boundary: Fires for API/Batch too—not only UI.

terminology.plain: One CDC message about a record change.
terminology.precise: Includes ChangeEventHeader (change type, entity) plus changed field data as defined for that object.
terminology.non_example: A Queueable execute is not a change event.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Gap/overflow events: neighboring CDC topics; do not invent their limits.
terminology.boundary: Subscribe via channel for the object or the all-changes channel.

terminology.plain: Writers emit; listeners react without sharing the writer's transaction.
terminology.precise: Decoupled near-real-time integration via the event bus rather than same-save DML or a single async job.
terminology.example: ERP subscribes to shipment CDC; warehouse Flow subscribes to LAB_Allocator_Requested__e.
terminology.non_example: Before-save Flow updating the same record.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Async Apex: one job, one governor pool.
terminology.boundary: Does not replace sharing or CRUD on subscriber DML.

terminology.plain: Send the event only if the parent save commits.
terminology.precise: Ties the message to Apex transaction success (APEX-010).
terminology.example: Order event published after LAB_Order__c insert commits.
terminology.non_example: Publish Immediately for a log that must survive rollback.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: Queueable enqueue: also dropped on rollback.
terminology.boundary: Default choice for business data signals.

terminology.plain: Send even if the parent transaction later fails.
terminology.precise: Useful for logging; dangerous if subscribers DML the same rows (lock/race). Immediate EventBus.publish calls: 150 per transaction.
terminology.example: LAB_Error_Log__e published in a catch before rethrow.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: After-commit publish counted as DML on the governors page.
terminology.boundary: Needs verification of current Considerations wording in the org's API version.

terminology.plain: Apex API to publish platform event instances.
terminology.precise: Immediate publishes: 150 per transaction. After-commit publishes participate in DML counting per the governors footnote.
terminology.boundary: Do not invent a daily EventBus.publish org cap from this method name.

terminology.precise: Apex trigger on the event, Flow, Pub/Sub API, CometD, empApi, event relay. Each subscriber does its own work and governors.
terminology.example: Apex trigger on LAB_Allocator_Requested__e enqueues Queueable.
terminology.non_example: A validation rule is not a subscriber.
terminology.confusable_neighbor: CDC channel vs custom event channel.
terminology.boundary: Subscriber DML is a new context—do not assume it shares the publisher's savepoint.

when_to_use: When multiple consumers must react to record changes: enable Change Data Capture on that object rather than N triggers calling N Queueables.
When you need a custom signal with your own fields: define a platform event and publish it from Apex or Flow.
When the listener must not run if the parent transaction rolls back: Publish After Commit (event-driven processing aligned with APEX-010).
When a log/diagnostic signal must leave the bus even if DML fails: Publish Immediately, with lock awareness.
When an external ERP should subscribe via Pub/Sub API instead of polling SOQL.
When you must cite EventBus.publish 150 for immediate events from Execution Governors and Limits.
when_not_to_use: Do not use platform events for a same-record field update that before-save Flow already handles.
Do not use Change Data Capture as a substitute for one Queueable callout—you will publish on every ETL touch.
Do not use Publish Immediately for inventory or payment signals that must match committed data.
Do not invent daily event-bus allocations; read Platform Event Allocations or mark Needs verification.
Do not treat the event bus as a transaction savepoint or FOR UPDATE replacement.
Do not subscribe in Apex and then DML the publisher's row without a lock/recursion plan.

interview_questions.question: Platform events versus Change Data Capture?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: CDC emits standard change events for CUD and undelete on selected objects. A platform event is a custom message you define and publish. Both ride the event bus; the schema and when they fire differ.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I use CDC when an ERP must see every LAB_Shipment__c change including Data Loader. I use a custom __e when the payload is a business signal, not a row diff. I mention API 44.0 for CDC and Customize Application plus API Enabled to define events. I do not invent daily allocations.
tradeoffs: Volume of CDC vs curated events

interview_questions.question: Publish After Commit versus Publish Immediately?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: After Commit emits only if the Apex transaction commits. Immediately can notify subscribers even if later DML rolls back. Immediate EventBus.publish is 150 per transaction.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I default After Commit for business data so warehouses do not allocate stock for a failed order. I use Immediately for log-style events. I warn that subscribers DML'ing the same row can lock. After-commit publish counts as DML per the governors footnote.
interview_questions.example: Failed LAB_Order__c validation: After Commit sends nothing; Immediately already fired.

interview_questions.question: ERP needs all shipment changes; warehouse needs only submit signals. Design it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: CDC on LAB_Shipment__c for the ERP. Custom After Commit event for submit. Queueable for the HTTP allocator if you need a job Id.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I refuse CDC-on-Order as the warehouse feed if 90% of updates are drafts. I refuse a trigger HTTP callout. I document that nightly shipment Batch will produce CDC volume. I keep event fields as a versioned contract.
interview_questions.example: LAB_Shipment__ChangeEvent to ERP; LAB_Allocator_Requested__e to warehouse trigger → Queueable.

interview_questions.question: Subscribers updated an order that later rolled back. What do you check?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Publish Immediately, or a subscriber that DML'd mid-save. Move to After Commit and keep subscriber work async.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I look at publish behavior, subscriber trigger, and lock errors. I do not blame Pub/Sub first. I add a test that throws after publish and asserts no LAB_Work__c for After Commit.
interview_questions.example: Immediately published allocator event created warehouse work for a draft that failed required fields.
tradeoffs: Immediate logs vs immediate business DML

interview_questions.question: When would you refuse platform events entirely?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Same-record updates, one Queueable worker, or when CDC volume would drown allocations. Events are for decoupling, not for replacing before-save Flow.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I walk AUTO-001 / APEX-011 / this topic. If the only consumer is one Apex class we own, a Queueable is simpler to monitor. If the object is chatty under ETL, I will not enable CDC without a volume review. I will not invent a bus cap to scare the room; I will say Needs verification and open allocations.
interview_questions.example: Status formula on the same LAB_Order__c: before-save Flow, not __e.

interview_questions.question: EventBus.publish throws a limit exception. Walk it.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: If the event is immediate, you may have hit 150 publishes in the transaction. If after commit, you may be hitting DML 150. Daily bus allocations are a different table—do not mix them.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I count publishes in the loop, check publish behavior, and look at Limits methods. I batch signals or move to CDC instead of publishing per field. I re-open Execution Governors and Limits rather than quoting a blog.
interview_questions.example: Loop of 200 EventBus.publish on an Immediately event during a Data Loader trigger.
tradeoffs: Loop vs one event with a list payload—if the schema allows

interview_questions.question: How do events relate to Apex transactions and Queueable?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: After-commit events follow the transaction. Queueable enqueue also dies on rollback. Immediately events can escape the unit. Subscribers run in their own context, not in your savepoint.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw three boxes: parent transaction, event bus, subscriber/async. I refuse to say 'events are just async Apex.' I mention EventBus.publish 150 for immediate and DML counting for after-commit. I point APEX-010 for savepoints and APEX-011 for job types.
interview_questions.example: Trigger publishes After Commit then enqueueJob; exception: neither event nor job survives.
follow_ups: Do savepoints roll back after-commit publishes?
weak_answer_warnings: Collapsing all async into one word

interview_questions.question: What do you refuse to memorize about event limits?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Unofficial daily delivery numbers, replay hours, and add-on packs. I will cite EventBus.publish 150 from the Apex governors page and send allocations to the current Platform Event Allocations topic.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Interviewers respect 'I will look it up' more than a fake 25,000. I know where the official tables live. I still know the per-transaction 150 because it is on the Apex governors page we already use for DML and enqueue.
interview_questions.example: Someone quotes a 2021 blog daily cap; you open the current allocations page instead.
tradeoffs: Memorized stale numbers vs cited pages
